messages.text: Did you see? XYZ is up 40% this week 🚀
My cousin's leading room says it doubles by June
I'm putting my whole bonus in
What's there to lose? It only goes up 😎

steps.title: 27 · office worker in Seoul
steps.body: Ji-woo saved **₩10,000,000** (about €6,800) over three years. Her chat is full of winners. Before she decides, let's see what a big price [[volatility|swing]] really does to money.

steps.prompt: XYZ rose 40% in one week. The next week it fell 40%. Where is Ji-woo's money compared with the start?
steps.reveal: ₩10M → ₩14M → ₩8.4M. The 40% drop is taken from a bigger amount than the 40% rise was, so the same percent up and down never lands back at zero.

steps.prompt: After a loss, how much must the price rise just to get back to the start? Find the loss that needs a +100% gain.

goal.hint: Think of losing half the money.

steps.title: Losses weigh more than gains
steps.body: −10% needs +11% to recover. −50% needs +100%. −80% needs +400%. That is the maths of a [[drawdown]]: the deeper the fall, the harder the climb back.

steps.prompt: Why doesn't +40% followed by −40% bring Ji-woo back to zero?
options: The −40% is taken from a bigger amount than the +40% was
The bank charges a fee in between
Prices always fall faster than they rise
steps.explanation: ₩10M × 1.4 × 0.6 = ₩8.4M. The second percent applies to the new, larger amount, so the same-sized drop removes more won.

steps.prompt: XYZ fell 50%. What rise does it need to get back to its old price?
steps.explanation: Half the money has to double to be whole again: ₩5M × 2 = ₩10M.

goal.hint: Try −50%: the money is cut in half.

t1.body: Ji-woo saved **₩10,000,000** (about €6,800) in three years. Her friends say they are winning a lot. Let's see what happens to money when a price goes up and down fast. This is called [[volatility]].

p1.prompt: A share price went up 40%. A week later it went down 40%. Is Ji-woo back where she started? Guess her result.
p1.reveal: She is at −16%. ₩10M became ₩14M, then ₩8.4M. The second 40% was taken from more money, so it took away more.

s1.prompt: If you lose money, the price must go up more than it went down to get it back. Move the slider. Find the loss that needs +100% to get back.

t2.title: Losing is harder to fix than winning
t2.body: Lose 10%, and you need +11% to get back. Lose half, and you need to double your money. The bigger the fall (a [[drawdown]]), the harder it is to get back.

q1.prompt: Up 40%, then down 40%. Why is Ji-woo not back at the start?
options: The 40% loss is taken from more money than the 40% gain
q1.explanation: ₩10M went up to ₩14M. 40% of ₩14M is more than 40% of ₩10M. So she ends with ₩8.4M.

q2.prompt: A price fell by half. How much must it go up to get back?
q2.explanation: Half must double to be whole again: ₩5M × 2 = ₩10M.
